model_output_raw.confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear pattern of an authorized user (user_04) with 'read_only' access and a baseline of 0 downloads per day performing 6 file downloads. Crucially, this user accessed files outside their department (Engineering projects) and worked significantly outside their normal hours (until 19:00). This behavior deviates sharply from their baseline and role, indicating a likely insider threat/data exfiltration.

attack_chain.description: user_04 logs in from normal IP within normal hours.
user_04 performs first file download (accounts_receivable), violating baseline of 0 downloads/day.
user_04 performs second file download (accounts_payable), establishing a pattern of bulk data collection.
user_04 accesses cross-department data (project_alpha), expanding scope beyond Finance.
user_04 downloads sensitive tax data, continuing the exfiltration pattern.
user_04 accesses second cross-department project (project_beta), indicating broad reconnaissance or data gathering.
user_04 downloads bank reconciliation data, a high-value financial asset.
user_04 downloads general ledger, a comprehensive financial record.
user_04 accesses cross-department data again at 17:15, outside normal working hours (09:00-17:00).
user_04 logs out at 19:00, having worked 2 hours past their scheduled shift.

gaps: No metadata (ticket numbers or justification) provided for the cross-department access or off-hours work.
No network traffic logs to confirm if the downloaded files were actually exfiltrated to an external destination.
No information on whether user_04 has a legitimate business need for the specific engineering project files accessed.
model_output_raw.narrative: user_04, a junior accountant with read-only access and a baseline of zero daily downloads, engaged in a systematic data exfiltration campaign. The user downloaded six sensitive financial files and accessed engineering project data outside their department, continuing activity two hours past their scheduled shift. This pattern of behavior strongly indicates an insider threat rather than legitimate maintenance or work.
